title: A 3D Bioprinted Pseudo-Bone Drug Delivery Scaffold for Bone Tissue Engineering.
summary: ANN-supported optimization selected a 3D-printed simvastatin scaffold with 20-day in-vitro release. The abstract reports hardness and resilience near healthy bone in a mechanically fractured human clavicle model. These release and ex-vivo mechanical endpoints do not establish living-organism healing or clinical benefit.
ai_technology: Artificial neural network for scaffold optimization

evidence.tested: Thirty-nine scaffold formulations were evaluated with ANN-supported optimization. The selected 14% PPF/16% PF127 formulation released simvastatin in vitro for 20 days. The abstract reports hardness and resilience near healthy bone in a mechanically fractured human clavicle model; specimen and replicate counts were not assessed in this review.
evidence.unknown: Living-organism bone healing and patient benefit are not established by the reported in-vitro release and ex-vivo mechanical model. Specimen and replicate counts were not assessed.
evidence.ai_role: A multilayer feed-forward/back-propagation artificial neural network optimized scaffold formulation using thermogelation and drug-release responses; it did not test biological healing.

source_review.scope: Publisher abstract and indexed publisher Methods/Results passages on ANN/formulations and drug release; complete article and mechanical-model methods not independently reviewed.
